## The system as a graph

```mermaid
flowchart TB
```

A command is accepted by the component that owns its context, emits the events one of its outcomes declares, and a dashed edge is a binding carrying an event into the next command. Design §9 begins one step earlier, at the actor who invokes the first command, and so does this graph: a solid edge out of an actor is a grant, and an actor drawn with no edge at all may invoke nothing — which is something the model says, not an arrow somebody forgot.

## Bounded contexts

- **[connection](./domains/connectors_prometheus-connection.md)** (`connectors_prometheus.connection`) — The Prometheus local connection — its native configuration, the `prometheus.bearer` profile and the configured identity probe that proves a credential. Eight types, no entities, no views, no commands, no events, no errors and no actors.
- **[reads](./domains/connectors_prometheus-reads.md)** (`connectors_prometheus.reads`) — Prometheus-owned PromQL instant and range selections, their result kinds and series bounds. Four types, no entities, no views, no commands, no events, no errors and no actors.
- **[rules](./domains/connectors_prometheus-rules.md)** (`connectors_prometheus.rules`) — Prometheus-owned alerting and recording rules as `rules.list` returns them, one record per rule. Five types, no entities, no views, no commands, no events, no errors and no actors.

## Components

A component is a unit of ownership, not a deployment. How many of each runs, and what each needs, is [the topology](./topology.md).
